findings: Historical adverse capture remains valid: NetworkService was blocked in TaskTracker::CompleteShutdown with three accounted shutdown-blocking items; individual task sources were not identified.
The exact current native source tree is unchanged from the retained baseline binary source used in this reversal.
The ordinary pre-fix host completed 42 of 42 fresh/reused launches with 42 positively qualified macOS helper/clone cleanups.
A global-request-context drain candidate also completed 42 of 42, but the unchanged baseline already passed and had the lower observed shutdown tail; the candidate is rejected rather than merged.
No adverse run was observed in this finite current-source plan. The causal-correction gate remains unmet; shipping a speculative workaround would violate the issue acceptance contract.

reviewQualificationFailures.disposition: Retain both failures independently of the watchdog investigation and of later qualification outcomes. No runtime fix or root cause is inferred.

releaseBoundary: Historical failures remain regression evidence. Any recurrence of watchdog exit 2 under current source is a release-reliability failure and should be captured with the maintained phase-triggered diagnostics before code changes.
limitations: Finite local execution is not proof the historical Chromium/macOS failure can never recur.
No individual Chromium blocking TaskSource was identified because no current adverse run was observed.
This record is not issue closure, a performance claim, production signing qualification, or proof that Chromium contains no shutdown defects.
